## Summary

64-bit data bus, 32 KB instruction cache, 128 KB 3-ported data cache, 64-byte memory bursts, a 1024-entry branch target cache.

## Details

- 64bit memory Data-bus.
- 32kb ICache , 1cycle=32byte to CPU every cycle.
- 128kb DCache 3ported. (3 access to Dcache per cycle)
- 1cycle=8byte read AND 8 byte write to/from CPU AND talk to mem.
- mem burst=64byte. latency is around 12 CPU cyle.
- 1024 entry BTC branch target cache.
- The CPU itself detect continuous memory access and will automatically prefetch the memory.
- 080 has selfmodify detection. This means writing to code that is in instruction-cache or is in the pipeline to be executed.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The cache sizes, the 64-bit data bus and the automatic prefetch are 68080 specific; don't reuse 68060 cache assumptions.

## Do / Don't

- DO rely on the automatic prefetch for sequential memory access; use TOUCH for non-sequential access.
